parts.title: Task 1 · Long reading: choose a title
parts.instruction: You have 2 hours for Reading and Writing together. Read the article about a community garden. Choose the best title for each paragraph (questions 1 to 5). There are six titles, but you only need five. Use each title once.

texts.label: Magazine article
texts.title: My garden in the city
paras: Last spring I moved to Leeds for a new job. I knew nobody in the city, and my flat had no garden. At weekends I was often alone and I felt a bit sad. One Saturday I walked past a small green space behind the library. A sign on the gate said: "Community garden - new members welcome."

The garden belongs to the people who work in it. About thirty people come, and they are of all ages. The youngest member is seven and the oldest is eighty-one. Everyone has a small space, called a plot, and pays £10 a year for it. The money buys tools, seeds and a new water tank.

My first plot was a mess. It was full of weeds and stones. An older neighbour, Mr Hall, showed me how to clean the ground. He told me to start with easy plants. I grew tomatoes, lettuces and a few herbs. Not everything was a success. The slugs ate most of my lettuces in June.

The best part of the garden is the people. On Wednesday evenings we have tea and cake together, and every month we cook a meal with the vegetables. I now know more than twenty people in Leeds. Two of them are good friends, and we often go walking on Sundays.

Next year I want to try something new. The group is planning a small shop outside the gate, and I have offered to work in it on Saturday mornings. I also want to grow pumpkins. If you live near a community garden, go and visit it. You don't need to know anything about plants.

pool.c: Feeling alone in a new city

parts.title: Task 2 · Multi-text reading: which text?
parts.instruction: Read the three texts about free-time activities in Stroud. For questions 19 to 23, decide which text (A, B or C) each sentence is about. You can use a text more than once.

texts.label: Text A · Poster
texts.title: Stroud Leisure Centre: adult swimming lessons
paras: Can't swim? Or do you want to swim better? Join our friendly adult classes.
Beginners: Monday evenings, 7.00 to 8.00 pm. Improvers: Thursday mornings, 10.00 to 11.00 am.
Each course lasts eight weeks and costs £64. Please bring a towel and a swimming cap. Lockers need a £1 coin.
Our teachers are all qualified, and there are never more than eight people in a class. To book a place, come to the front desk or phone 01632 960 214.

texts.label: Text B · Review
texts.title: My first month at the Stroud Community Kitchen (by Tom Warren)
paras: I joined the Stroud Community Kitchen in September. It meets on Wednesday evenings in the old school hall. Each session costs £8, and the food is included.
Last week we made Thai curry. The teacher, Mrs Okoye, explained every step slowly, so I never felt lost. There were twelve of us, and we ate the meal together at the end.
The only problem is the car park, which is very small. I now come by bus, and the number 9 stops outside. It is a lovely way to meet people, and I am going to bring my sister next time.

texts.label: Text C · Email
texts.title: Email from Jo
paras: Hi Ana,

You asked about free-time ideas in Stroud. My favourite is the Hill Walkers group. We meet at the station at 9.30 every Saturday morning and walk for about three hours. It is free, but you must wear good shoes.
Last Saturday we climbed Cam Peak and had a picnic at the top. There are about twenty members, and some bring their dogs. Nobody is too slow! We stop for a rest every half hour.
If you want to come, just send me a message. Bring water and a coat, because it often rains.
Jo

items.prompt: Which text tells you how to book a place by phone?
Which text mentions travelling by bus?
Which text says what kind of shoes you need?
Which text gives the largest number of people allowed in one group?
Which text talks about a problem with parking?

parts.title: Task 3 · Reading into writing
parts.instruction: Use information from all three texts from Task 2 to answer the question. Write 70 to 100 words in your own words. Do not copy whole sentences from the texts.

tasks.title: Task 3 · An email to Ana
tasks.situation:
You have read three texts about free-time activities in Stroud.
Text A: Adult swimming lessons at the leisure centre. Eight weeks, £64. Beginners on Monday evenings, improvers on Thursday mornings. Never more than eight people in a class.
Text B: Stroud Community Kitchen. Wednesday evenings, £8 a session, food included. Twelve people cook and eat together.
Text C: Hill Walkers. Free. Saturdays at 9.30 at the station, about three hours, about twenty members.
Your friend Ana has just moved to Stroud. She wants to meet new people and try something new.
tasks.prompt: Write an email to Ana. Say which of the three activities you think is best for her and why. Use information from all three texts.
points: Why is it a good idea for Ana? (use the text)
One thing about each of the other two activities (cost, time or people)
tasks.model: Hi Ana, I think the Hill Walkers group is the best idea for you. It is free, and about twenty people come, so you can meet many new friends. They meet at the station on Saturdays at 9.30 and walk for about three hours. The swimming lessons are good if you want to learn something, but they cost £64 and the classes are small. The Community Kitchen costs £8 each time, but you cook and eat a meal with twelve people. Try one first! Love, Sam
checklist: Task: you choose one activity and give reasons, and you mention information from all three texts.
Own words: you do not copy whole sentences from the texts; you change the words or put the facts together in a new way.
Organisation: a greeting, a clear recommendation, reasons, and a closing line.
Language: short, correct sentences; the reader understands everything, even if there are small mistakes.

parts.title: Task 4 · Extended writing
parts.instruction: Write a review of 70 to 100 words. Answer all four points.

tasks.title: Task 4 · A review of a café or restaurant
tasks.situation: A website for visitors to your town wants reviews from local people. You decide to write about a café or a restaurant you visited recently.
tasks.prompt: Write a review of a café or restaurant you visited. Say what you liked and what you did not like.
points: Where is it and when did you go?
What did you eat or drink?
What did you like? Was there a problem?
Do you recommend it? Why or why not?
tasks.model: Last Saturday I went to a new café called The Green Spoon in Bath with my sister. It is near the river, and the staff are very friendly. I had vegetable soup with fresh bread, and my sister had a big piece of chocolate cake. Everything was tasty, but we had to wait twenty minutes for our drinks. The prices are fair: lunch for two cost £18. I liked the garden very much. I would recommend this café to anyone who wants a nice lunch with friends. I will go again soon.
checklist: Task: all four points are answered with a few details.
Organisation: the review has a beginning, a middle and an end; linking words such as and, but, because help the reader.
Language: past tense for what happened (went, had, liked), present tense for your opinion; mostly correct spelling.

parts.title: Talk 1 · Cycling to work
parts.instruction: You will hear a short talk. You hear it twice. In the exam you answer the examiner's questions aloud; here, write a short answer for questions 1 to 6.

clips.title: Talk 1 · Ruth's new way to work

script.t: Hello, my name is Ruth, and I want to tell you about my new way to get to work. Until March I went to work by car. My office is in Derby, eight miles from my home. The car cost a lot of money, and the traffic was terrible. So in April I bought a bicycle. It was second-hand and cost two hundred and fifty pounds. Now I leave home at ten past seven, and I arrive at twenty to eight. That is a little faster than the car! I cycle along the canal for most of the way, and I often see ducks. The only problem is the rain. On wet days I take a spare shirt in my bag. My colleague Ben cycles too, so we ride together on Fridays. I feel much healthier now, and I save about forty pounds a month.

items.prompt: How did Ruth go to work until March?
How far is her office from her home?
How much was the bicycle?
What time does Ruth leave home?
Where does she cycle for most of the way?
What does she take with her on wet days?
accept: a spare shirt in her bag

parts.title: Talk 2 · A visit to a city farm
parts.instruction: You will hear a second short talk. You hear it twice. First say what the talk is about (question 7), then answer questions 8 to 13 with a short answer.

clips.title: Talk 2 · Welcome to Hilltop City Farm

script.t: Hello everyone, and welcome to Hilltop City Farm. My name is Kareem, and I look after the animals here. The farm opens at nine o'clock and closes at five, every day except Monday. Entry is free, but we ask you to give two pounds if you can. We have about forty animals: sheep, goats, pigs and ducks. The most popular animal is Daisy, our oldest pig. She is twelve years old. At eleven o'clock, children can feed the goats. At two o'clock there is a short talk about bees in the garden. The café is next to the main gate, and it sells cakes made on the farm. Please do not give the animals your own food. If you need help, ask a person in a green T-shirt. We hope you enjoy your day.

items.question: What is the talk about?
options: A welcome to a city farm for visitors
A cooking class in a café
A job interview for a farm worker

parts.title: Topic discussion
parts.instruction: Before the exam you choose a topic and prepare it. In the exam you tell the examiner about it, and then you talk about it together. Use the card to practise: prepare four points, then speak for about one minute. Answer the examiner's questions.

tasks.title: Topic discussion · My favourite sport
tasks.situation: How to prepare: choose something you know well and like (a hobby, a place, a person, your job). Write four points as short notes, not whole sentences. Think of one detail or example for each point and learn the key words. Do not learn a long speech by heart: the examiner will ask questions, and you must answer them.

card.title: Sample topic: My favourite sport (cycling)
lines: 1. What it is and how often I do it
4. What I want to do next

redemittel: I do this once / twice a week.
Sorry, could you say that again, please?
tasks.model:
My topic is cycling. I cycle three times a week, usually in the evening, and on Sundays I go for a long ride. I started two years ago. My brother gave me his old bike, and I went out with him every weekend. I like cycling because I can be outside and I feel free. It is also good for my health, and it is cheap. Next summer I want to cycle from Bristol to Bath with my friends. It is about twenty-five miles.
Examiner: Do you ride alone or with other people?
Candidate: Mostly with my brother, but sometimes alone. I like both.
Examiner: What do you need for cycling?
Candidate: A good helmet, a light for the evening and a bottle of water. A warm coat in winter is important too.
checklist: Topic: you cover your four points and give one detail for each.
Interaction: you listen to the examiner's questions and answer them directly, not with a prepared speech.
Language: simple, correct sentences with because, and and but; the verbs are in the right tense.
Delivery: you speak clearly and not too fast; you ask the examiner to repeat a question if you did not understand.

parts.title: Conversation
parts.instruction: The examiner chooses a subject area and asks you questions. You do not prepare this part. Answer in full sentences and add a reason or an example. Practise with the questions on the card.

tasks.title: Conversation · Travel
tasks.situation: Subject area: Travel. The examiner starts with an easy question and then asks about your experience and your plans. Listen carefully, answer, and add one more detail.

card.title: Typical examiner questions: Travel
lines: How do you usually travel to work or school?
Do you like travelling by train? Why or why not?
Tell me about a journey you remember.
Where would you like to go on holiday next?
What do you take with you on a long journey?

redemittel: I would like to go to … because …
tasks.model:
Examiner: How do you usually travel to work?
Candidate: I usually go by bus. It takes about thirty minutes. Sometimes I walk when the weather is nice.
Examiner: Tell me about a journey you remember.
Candidate: Last summer I went to Scotland by train with my cousin. The train was very long, but the view was beautiful. We saw mountains and a lot of sheep. I remember it because it rained for three days, but we still had a great time.
Examiner: Where would you like to go next?
Candidate: I would like to go to Cornwall. I have never seen the sea there, and my friends say the beaches are lovely.
Examiner: What do you take with you on a long journey?
Candidate: I always take a book, some water and a sandwich.
checklist: Communication: you answer every question and add a reason, a detail or an example.
Interaction: you react to what the examiner says; you ask for repetition if needed.
Language: past tense for the journey (went, saw, rained), would like to for plans; few mistakes that stop the examiner understanding you.
Delivery: clear pronunciation, a steady speed, and no long silences.
